BIOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: BIOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Excretion and Homeostasis in Animals Page 12 of 48 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AN? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Excretion and Homeostasis in Animals Page 12 of 48 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AN.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Excretion and Homeostasis in Animals Page 12 of 48 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AN.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion and Homeostasis in Animals Page 12 of 48 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AN.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Excretion and Homeostasis in Animals Page 12 of 48 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AN.

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 37 °C

3. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growth and Development in Plants ● Meaning of growth and development ● Structure? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growth and Development in Plants ● Meaning of growth and development ● Structure.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growth and Development in Plants ● Meaning of growth and development ● Structure.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Growth and Development in Plants ● Meaning of growth and development ● Structure.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growth and Development in Plants ● Meaning of growth and development ● Structure.

6. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Excretion in Plants ● Meaning and importance of excretion (include reasons why p? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Excretion in Plants ● Meaning and importance of excretion (include reasons why p.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Excretion in Plants ● Meaning and importance of excretion (include reasons why p.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Excretion in Plants ● Meaning and importance of excretion (include reasons why p.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Excretion in Plants ● Meaning and importance of excretion (include reasons why p.

8. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

9. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cell Division ● Meaning of cell division and structure of chromosomes ● Types of? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell Division ● Meaning of cell division and structure of chromosomes ● Types of.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Cell Division ● Meaning of cell division and structure of chromosomes ● Types of.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cell Division ● Meaning of cell division and structure of chromosomes ● Types of.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cell Division ● Meaning of cell division and structure of chromosomes ● Types of.

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Producers
   D. Primary consumers only

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ecology ● Ecosystems ● Adaptations of organisms to different habitats (xerophyte? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ecology ● Ecosystems ● Adaptations of organisms to different habitats (xerophyte.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ecology ● Ecosystems ● Adaptations of organisms to different habitats (xerophyte.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Ecology ● Ecosystems ● Adaptations of organisms to different habitats (xerophyte.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ecology ● Ecosystems ● Adaptations of organisms to different habitats (xerophyte.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Taxonomy I ● Meaning and significance of taxonomy ● Taxonomic units and nomencla and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Ecology ● Ecosystems ● Adaptations of organisms to different habitats (xerophyte and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Taxonomy II ● Kingdom Plantae (general characteristics of organisms in Divisions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Cell Division ● Meaning of cell division and structure of chromosomes ● Types of and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
